The '''Ishimori equation''' is a [[partial differential equation]] proposed by the Japanese [[mathematician]] {{harvtxt|Ishimori|1984}}. Its interest is as the first example of a nonlinear spin-one field model in the plane that is [[integrable system|integrable]] {{harv|Sattinger|Tracy|Venakides|1991|p=78}}.

==Equation==
The Ishimori equation has the form
{{NumBlk||<math display="block"> \frac{\partial \mathbf{S}}{\partial t} = \mathbf{S}\wedge \left(\frac{\partial^2 \mathbf{S}}{\partial x^2} + \frac{\partial^2 \mathbf{S}}{\partial y^2}\right)+ \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}\frac{\partial \mathbf{S}}{\partial y} + \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}\frac{\partial \mathbf{S}}{\partial x},</math>|{{EquationRef|1a}}}}
{{NumBlk||<math display="block"> \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}-\alpha^2 \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial y^2}=-2\alpha^2 \mathbf{S} \cdot \left(\frac{\partial \mathbf{S}}{\partial x}\wedge \frac{\partial \mathbf{S}}{\partial y}\right).</math>|{{EquationRef|1b}}}}

==Lax representation==

The [[Lax representation]]
{{NumBlk||<math display="block">L_t = AL - LA</math>|{{EquationRef|2}}}}
of the equation is given by
{{NumBlk||<math display="block">L =\Sigma \partial_x + \alpha I\partial_y,</math>|{{EquationRef|3a}}}}
{{NumBlk||<math display="block">A = -2i\Sigma\partial_x^2+(-i\Sigma_x-i\alpha\Sigma_y\Sigma+u_yI-\alpha^3u_x\Sigma)\partial_x.</math>|{{EquationRef|3b}}}}

Here
{{NumBlk||<math display="block">\Sigma=\sum_{j=1}^3S_j\sigma_j,</math>|{{EquationRef|4}}}}
the <math>\sigma_i</math> are the [[Pauli matrices]] and <math>I</math> is the identity matrix.

==Reductions==
The Ishimori equation admits an important reduction:
in 1+1 dimensions it reduces to the [[Heisenberg model (classical)|continuous classical Heisenberg ferromagnet equation]] (CCHFE). The CCHFE is integrable.

==Equivalent counterpart==
The equivalent counterpart of the Ishimori equation is the [[Davey-Stewartson equation]].
